---
title: "Applied replication for data skills"
subtitle: "Housing and racial bias"
engine: knitr
format:
  live-revealjs:
    webr:
      # The packages that the helpers of the lab and the cells of the hands-on
      # slides call: dplyr and purrr in the helpers, parameters with sandwich
      # for the HC2 errors, marginaleffects for the logit and effectsize for
      # the conversion rule of the robustness study; datawizard in the cells of
      # Tasks 2, 3, 5 and 6; tinyplot for the figures of Tasks 2, 5 and 6 and for
      # the graph. The runtime adds evaluate, knitr and htmltools itself, and tibble
      # comes with dplyr. gt is left out, because no slide prints a formatted
      # table and it adds 12 to 23 seconds to the first opening of a page.
      packages:
        - dplyr
        - datawizard
        - purrr
        - tinyplot
        - parameters
        - sandwich
        - marginaleffects
        - effectsize
      repos:
        - https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-wasm
# The seven files that the cells read, fetched into the browser when the deck
# opens; the runtime drops the leading ../ of each path, so inside the browser
# they sit under data/, the folder that the setup cell below
# names as .data_dir.
resources:
  - ../data/housing_emails.csv
  - ../data/housing_original.csv
  - ../data/spec_curve.csv
  - ../data/menu_options.csv
  - ../data/dag_answers.csv
  - ../data/housing_replication.csv
  - ../data/replication_curve.csv
live:
  show-hints: true
  show-solutions: true
# Optional runs that this deck includes in its main flow (core-runs.lua
# strips their .deepdive mark); the others stay on the d toggle. The one run
# of this deck is "methods": the methods tutorial after the menu in Part 4,
# and the multiverse background after Task 4.
core-runs: []
# The format of the deck, which the segments of the Housing case study read
# through Quarto conditional content (when-meta="deck.short" and so on): one
# of short or day, and menu where the deck teaches the specification menu.
deck:
  day: true
  menu: true
# THE DECK OF THE FULL-DAY FORMAT, OF DAY 2 OF THE LONG FORMAT AND OF THE
# SELF-TAUGHT FORMAT
# - The participants of the full-day format do the six tasks in the workspace, in
#   their IDE. This deck carries the whole browser lab on its slides, through
#   the Quarto Live extension: the facilitator runs each step on the shared
#   screen, so that the class can compare its output with the slides, and a
#   participant whose installation fails carries on in the deck. Each
#   hands-on slide names the chunk or the file of the workspace that holds
#   the same step.
# - The hands-on segments in _segments/ (_handson1-live.qmd to
#   _handson4-submit-live.qmd, _defaults-live.qmd, _placement-live.qmd,
#   _prereg-live.qmd and _handson6-live.qmd) hold the cells of Tasks 1 to 6 of
#   lab.qmd, one step to a cell, with the hints and solutions
#   of its exercises. The helpers of the lab are
#   ../_includes/_lab-helpers.qmd and the graph helpers of Task 2
#   ../_includes/_lab-graph.qmd, both included after the setup cell that
#   names the data folder. The two setup segments stay in
#   ../slides/_segments/, because the decks of day 3 include them as well.
# - The setup cell and the helpers sit on the agenda slide, after its notes,
#   because a cell or a comment placed before the first heading of a deck
#   makes a slide of its own; they print nothing.
# - The part dividers keep the ids that the pages of the formats link.
# - No duration goes on any slide or into any note.
---
